newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, palladium leaps.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, palladium leaps.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures settled mixed on Thursday, with gold weaker on the yen's rebound while palladium futures continued to rocket as private investors were forced to cover their shorts, traders said.
October and December TOCOM palladium rocketed up by their 36 yen per gram daily limits by the close. Benchmark June was up 11 yen at 647 yen.
Benchmark June gold was off seven yen at 1,222 yen.
"Russian spot sales of palladium were lower than expected, which prompted private investors, facing margin calls, to cover their shorts," one trader said.

Platinum futures erased early gains on profit-taking, as the platinum market was not as tight as palladium, the traders said. Expectations that Japan's platinum demand for this year will dip slightly due to the slump in the jewellery sector, dampened sentiment in platinum.
Japanese traders received July PGM shipments from Russia last week, and said they were expecting the August PGM shipments around August 10.
Gold futures were pressured by the yen's rebound against the yen late in the day. Spot gold was quoted at $326.00/50 per ounce at 0745 GMT, against $325.80/30 in New York overnight.
In gold futures, activity was mainly dominated by inter-month trade by trading houses as private investors were generally sidelined amid uncertainty over the direction in the currency market.

"Recent volatility in currencies made private investors nervous," one trading house trader said. Both spot gold and TOCOM gold futures are likely to move within relatively narrow ranges for some time, the trader said.
Silver futures were mixed in thin trade. Benchmark June silver was down 1.2 yen per 10 grams at 168.3 yen.
